why: Every search starts from n and takes the nearest remaining branch on one side, so the next candidate on each side only ever moves outward. Two pointers, r moving right from n+1 and l moving left from n-1, skip zeros and pick alternately.
hints: After you take the nearest branch on the right, where does the next right search start looking?
Just past it: branches are removed, so the nearest remaining one on each side is further out. Keep r and l as outward-moving pointers, skipping zero cells.
Loop while total < 100: advance r and l past zeros, take the side whose turn it is (or the other side if it is exhausted), record the index, add the length, flip the turn. O(len(forest)).
pitfalls: The starting cell n is never collected, even if forest[n] > 0.
When one side is exhausted, the search switches to the other side; the alternation then continues from there.
Stop immediately once the total reaches 100 or more (>= 100, not > 100).
Return indices, not lengths, in pickup order.
